extracted.intended_audience: Extramural researchers applying to or awaiting NIH (NIGMS/NCI/NIA/etc.) grant funding (K99, R01, R21, SBIR/STTR, MIRA, etc.)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, procedural, and programmatic guidance for applicants and awardees about NIH post-review stages (deferral, council, JIT, pending admin review, award processing), PO/GMS interactions, transfers, and budgeting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact Program Officer about deferral/transfer/resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: If you receive a deferral or have questions about resubmission or relinquishing an application to a secondary IC, contact your NIGMS (or other IC) Program Officer to ask about the deferral, whether they would recommend relinquishing the application to the secondary IC, and whom to contact at the secondary IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask the PO whether the deferral is to allow a resubmission next year, whether the secondary IC would accept the application, and for resubmission advice if you haven't already requested it. Do not assume relinquishment should occur without confirming the secondary IC would accept the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral notification interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'deferral' notice can indicate that funding has been deferred (e.g., to give time to submit an amended application next year) rather than a decision not to fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask your PO for the specific reason for deferral; sometimes it is routine (e.g., to permit amendment/resubmission) rather than a negative finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: MIRA acceptance confirmation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: NIGMS may request an email stating you will accept a MIRA award to ensure applicants will accept the MIRA and decline any simultaneous competing R01s before administrative review begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This request signals NIGMS intends to fund your application (subject to administrative review). Responding affirms you will accept the MIRA, allowing NIGMS to proceed with more involved administrative review.

rubrics_metrics.name: PO vs GMS responsibilities and when to contact them
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Officers handle programmatic matters (resubmission advice, policy questions, transfers), while Grants Management Specialists (GMS) handle award processing and administrative issues (JIT, NOA preparation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact your PO for programmatic advice (resubmission, transfers); contact GMS only for award-processing items (e.g., JIT status). If you have questions about whether your JIT was received or what the GMS needs, check with the GMS. Recognize that PO is not involved in award processing and GMS may be extremely busy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive contact with PO/GMS during award processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not repeatedly contact POs or GMSs while awards are being processed; they are very busy and will contact you if they need information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist 'bugging' staff about routine pending statuses. If GMS requests JIT or documents, respond promptly; otherwise wait. Over-contacting will not speed processing and may be counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-Time (JIT) readiness and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: If JIT is requested, have documents ready and respond quickly; JIT is requested only when the IC is seriously considering an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit JIT promptly when asked; some JIT requests have very short turnarounds (same-day). Failing to meet a JIT deadline can cause an IC to skip your application in favor of the next one. You may also proactively submit JIT info so it's available if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal year award timing (Sept 30 deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs must obligate funds within the fiscal year; awards are often processed up through September 30 and can be issued late in the FY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards can be issued anytime up to Sept 30. Processing may accelerate at fiscal year end and is subject to appropriations timing; do not treat your proposed start date as a hard deadline—awards can be made earlier or later than that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select pay decision factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Select-pay (funding above the payline) determinations consider score ranking and programmatic interest, but other factors (e.g., administrative problems, JIT responsiveness) also influence which applications ultimately receive awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher-ranked apps can be skipped if administrative issues arise or JIT turnaround is slow; predicting select-pay outcomes can be difficult until the end of the FY. Communicate with your PO about resubmission strategy if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending administrative review meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: A status of 'pending administrative review' or 'pending' means the application is being processed for a possible award, assuming no additional administrative issues are uncovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You usually do not need to take action while pending; wait for GMS to request items. If pending due to others' award issues (e.g., mentor's awards), there may be nothing you can do and contacting GMS repeatedly is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferring K99/K-series awards and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: You should communicate early with your PO if you plan to change institutions; transfers are possible if the new institution offers comparable or better resources and an approved mentor, but certain moves (e.g., to a faculty position) will forfeit K99 eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PO approval and NIH approval of the new mentor/institution are required. If the new environment lacks required resources or an appropriate mentor, transfer will not be allowed. Discuss transfer plans before NOA; hiding moves from PO is ill-advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award start date may differ from proposed start date
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual award start date can be earlier or later than the start date proposed in your application; NIH can start awards before a proposed date or after it (within the FY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume the proposed start date limits when funds can be obligated; plan for variability and be prepared for earlier-than-expected starts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and salary adjustments at JIT
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot request more total funds at JIT than in the submitted application; increasing percent effort funded by NIH requires reallocating funds from other budget categories rather than receiving additional money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you requested 80% salary coverage in the application, you cannot later ask NIH to pay 100% without reducing other budget items. Mistakes or omissions in JIT (e.g., incorrect current salary) can result in NOA reflecting the submitted/current amounts; institutions often must negotiate post-award.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESI vs NI funding considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Early Stage Investigator (ESI) status receives special consideration at NIH; 'New Investigator' (NI) status does not receive the same special treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning team roles and PI status, know that ESI policies differ from NI; POs and ICs evaluate ESI support differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council review status meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Statuses like 'council review completed' indicate that Council has considered the application and are not, by themselves, a negative sign; they are stages of the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A change to 'council review completed' is procedural; funding decisions and next steps (e.g., JIT requests) will follow. Occasional status delays (e.g., 'council review pending' after the meeting) can reflect internal processing lags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of continuing resolutions on funding and paylines
rubrics_metrics.description: When the federal government is under a continuing resolution, ICs generally do not make routine new awards until a final appropriation is available; interim paylines (if used) are conservative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs avoid risking awards that might exceed a final appropriation. Interim paylines are typically lower than prior-year final paylines and can be raised retroactively after appropriation is finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain parallel submissions while awaiting A1/A0 outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: If an A1/A0 outcome is uncertain or likely to require select pay, maintain another application under review (e.g., submit another A0) to avoid losing time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your PO recommends preparing another submission, do so to preserve timing/options; waiting solely on a pending A1 can leave you without a fallback if funding does not materialize.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOA issuance and typical budget cuts
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of Award (NOAs) may include budget cuts (often standard); award amounts and possibly earlier-than-requested start dates can be adjusted in the NOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect budget reductions and plan contingencies. Including a proposed budget cut percentage in shared timelines can help others plan how to reduce budgets if awarded.
